title: Video and Animation in Milan: Explainers and Motion | 22 Signals
description: Video and animation in Milan for brands and manufacturers: product explainers, motion graphics, 2D and 3D animation and AI video, in versions for every market.
h1: Video and animation in Milan for products that are hard to explain in a photo
intro: We produce video and animation for Milan companies: product explainers, motion graphics, 2D and 3D animation, AI video and edited social content. Most of it is made from your existing material, drawings and 3D files, without a large shoot. Every film is cut in versions for each channel and market, with subtitles in the languages your buyers read.

sections.h: When a photograph is not enough
p: A sofa looks good in a photo. A sofa with a hidden mechanism that turns it into a bed, in forty fabrics, does not. The same goes for a packaging machine, a valve, a smart lighting system or a jacket with a removable lining. Buyers need to see how something works, and they need to see it quickly.

That is where video and animation in Milan companies earn their keep. A ninety-second animation can show what a sales engineer usually explains in a meeting, play on a loop at a trade fair stand, sit on the product page and go out in a LinkedIn campaign, all from one production.

list: Product explainers: how it works, how it is installed, what makes it different
Motion graphics: data, processes and services explained with animated type and diagrams
2D animation: character and illustration-led films for brands, training and campaigns
3D animation: products, machinery and interiors animated from CAD files or new models
AI video: concepts, backgrounds and variations produced quickly, then finished by editors
Social cuts: short vertical versions for Instagram, TikTok, YouTube Shorts and LinkedIn
Event content: loops for stands, screens and showroom displays

sections.h: Made for the way Milan sells
list: Furniture and design: mechanisms, materials and configurations animated for Salone del Mobile and dealer training
Fashion and accessories: motion pieces for collection launches, craftsmanship stories and product details for e-commerce
Machinery and industrial: animations that show inside a machine, how it fits a production line and how it is serviced
Financial and professional services: short explainers for products, processes and investor updates
Food and drink: origin stories and process films for export markets and trade buyers

p: Filming in a working plant is expensive and disruptive. Machines must stop, the space must be cleaned, and safety rules make many angles impossible. Animation avoids most of that. We build from the CAD files your engineers already have, add materials and lighting, and show views no camera could reach, such as a cutaway of a gearbox or the inside of a filling head.

Where real footage helps, such as craftspeople at work in a leather workshop or a family business telling its own story, we plan a short, focused shoot with a local crew and combine it with motion graphics and animation in the edit.

Milan exporters rarely need one video. They need an Italian version, an English master and often German, French, Spanish or Arabic subtitles or voiceover. We plan for that from the script stage: on-screen text kept short and easy to swap, graphics that do not depend on one language, and timings that leave room for longer translations.
Our team writes and produces in English. Italian scripts, subtitles and voiceover are arranged with native partners where you need them. Every version is checked against the master before delivery.

AI video tools now produce useful backgrounds, concepts and variations in hours rather than days. We use them where they save time without hurting quality: early concept boards, alternative scenes for testing in ads and background environments. For luxury and design brands, where every detail of the product matters, the product itself is built and animated properly. We also follow the platforms' disclosure rules and the EU AI Act's transparency requirements for synthetic content as they apply.

Some of the most useful films never appear in an advert. Italian manufacturers sell machines and systems to customers all over the world, and each customer needs to install, use and maintain them correctly. Short animated guides reduce support calls, cut the time technicians spend travelling and help distributors train their own staff in their own language.

The same applies inside the company. New staff in a showroom or a sales office learn a complex range faster from a set of short films than from a thick binder. We plan these as a library, with a consistent style and structure, so new chapters can be added as the range changes. Because the 3D models already exist from the marketing work, each new training film costs far less to make than the first.

sections.h: How a production runs: Talk, Plan, Build, Grow
list: Talk: a 15-minute call about what the film must achieve and where it will be shown.
Plan: script, style frames and a written production plan within 5 to 7 days.
Build: storyboard, animation and edit in rounds you review, with dates in writing.
Grow: cut-downs, translations and new versions as campaigns and results come in.

p: A film for Salone has to be ready before the doors open, not during the week. We plan backwards from the event, leave time for your review and translation, and deliver the files for screens, web and social at the same time. We have broadcast more than 20 live events, which teaches a healthy respect for dates that cannot move.

Reviews happen online through a shared review link where you comment on the exact frame, and calls are booked at times that suit your team. If a shoot is needed in Milan or at your plant, we plan it in the production schedule.

faqs.q: What does video and animation in Milan cost?
faqs.a: It depends on length, style and how many versions you need. A motion graphics explainer built from existing material costs less than a 3D film with new models. We price after the first call and set out each stage in writing.

faqs.q: Can you animate our products from CAD files?
faqs.a: Yes. Engineering CAD files are often the best starting point. We prepare them for animation, add materials and lighting, and protect any confidential detail you want hidden.
Yes. Our team produces in English, and Italian scripts, subtitles and voiceover are arranged with native partners. We plan graphics so language versions are easy to swap.

faqs.q: How long does an explainer take?
faqs.a: A short motion graphics explainer usually takes a few weeks from approved script to final files. 3D work takes longer. The exact dates go in the production plan.
When real footage is needed, we plan a focused shoot with a local crew in Milan or at your site. Many projects need no filming at all because animation covers what a camera would.

Where it saves time without hurting quality, yes, mainly for concepts, backgrounds and ad variations. Products are modelled and animated properly, and we follow disclosure rules for synthetic content.
